purpose: Script one real change through worktree create, structural diff review and cleanup, twice: once with worktrunk+difftastic, once with native git worktree+git diff, on a scratch repository, per gap_index 8's next_check as narrowed by this wave's unit brief ('one scripted change end-to-end (worktree, structural diff, cleanup; no push)'). `gh pr create`/`merge` is explicitly NOT executed: this wave's authorization forbids pushing except where a unit task names a scratch branch, and this task names no such exception, so the GitHub-PR leg of the ORIGINAL gap 8 text ('across worktree creation, structural review, PR handling and cleanup') is out of scope here and recorded as not_run rather than silently omitted or faked.
preregistered: Both arms perform: init scratch repo, create a worktree/branch for a feature change, edit compute.py to add a None-skipping guard, run the arm's diff tool, commit the change ON THE FEATURE BRANCH (not merged to main, since no PR merge step runs), then clean up the worktree via the arm's own tool. If arm A (worktrunk) and arm B (native git) both complete all steps and leave a clean single-worktree final state, that would be a clean tie on E2E mechanics (with difftastic's structural report scored as at least as informative as git diff's line-based one, from the larger-fixture and gap-6 receipts). If either arm fails a step it would not otherwise fail (i.e. a step whose semantics are the same across arms), that is recorded as a genuine reliability/ergonomics difference, not retried or worked around beyond what a real user would naturally try. This check does not predict which arm will 'win'.

arm_b_git_worktree_git_diff.failure_detail: `git branch -d feature-change` refused: 'the branch feature-change is not fully merged'. This is CORRECT, safe git behavior (matches worktrunk's own underlying safety judgment of retaining an unmerged branch). CORRECTED (fix round, 2026-09-23): e2e_compare.py (line 116) adds a 'cleanup-delete-branch' step ONLY to arm B's script; arm A's script (line 113) has no matching step that attempts a branch delete. So this is not a case where arm A succeeded at a step and arm B failed the same step -- the step exists in only one arm's script. A post-hoc `git branch -a` (added in the fix round) shows arm A's and arm B's repos end in the IDENTICAL final git state: worktree removed, `feature-change` branch retained, unmerged. This receipt's own preregistration says a failure counts only 'on a step whose semantics are the same across arms'; a step present in only one arm's script does not meet that bar, so this is not scored as a tool difference.

result.comparison_summary: Both arms produced a correct, non-empty diff report on the same scripted change; difftastic's report was structurally parsed and smaller (273 vs 343 bytes) for the same 6-line Python edit, consistent with prior larger-fixture findings. CORRECTED (fix round, 2026-09-23): the originally claimed 'decisive difference' in cleanup ergonomics is an artifact of the script giving arm B an extra step (an explicit `git branch -d` attempt) that arm A's script never runs, not a difference in the underlying tools' end states -- both arms leave the worktree removed and the unmerged branch retained. This E2E run is therefore a tie/inconclusive on cleanup mechanics as executed; it does not establish that worktrunk's single-command remove is functionally superior to native git's two-command remove+branch-d sequence for THIS scenario, only that a real user driving native git through the equivalent two commands would encounter (and need to consciously resolve) an extra decision point that worktrunk's single command absorbs silently -- a genuine but more modest ergonomics observation than 'decisive', not independently re-verified with a matched two-arm script in this wave.
